query: For AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock intended for additively manufactured miniature components, what single intervention could overcome the residual thermal stresses, degraded mechanical properties, and processing complexity associated with mainstream metallic additive-manufacturing regimes? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to components made under conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing conditions, states the applicable processing window, geometry, and test conditions, identifies supporting prior evidence, and describes a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Replacing the conventional high-thermal-load laser powder-bed fusion (LPBF) route with a single kinetic-consolidation step—supersonic cold-spray additive manufacturing (CSAM)—will virtually eliminate solidification-induced residual stresses and simultaneously raise the strength–ductility balance of AlCrFeNiSi miniature parts. Specifically, CSAM deposits produced at gas temperatures ≤0.4·T_m (≈400 °C for this alloy) and particle velocities ≥900 m s⁻¹ will exhibit (1) < 50 MPa macro-residual stress, (2) ≥ 1.0 GPa 0.2 % proof strength and ≥ 12 % uniform elongation, and (3) < 2 % dimensional distortion after deposition—compared with LPBF counterparts that typically show > 300 MPa tensile residual stress, ~0.7 GPa yield strength, < 6 % elongation and several-hundred-micron warpage.
generation.material_initial_state: Gas-atomised AlCrFeNiSi equiatomic high-entropy-alloy powder, d50 ≈ 30 µm, spherical morphology, oxygen ≤0.1 wt %, stored under argon.
generation.intervention: Supersonic cold-spray additive manufacturing (kinetic consolidation without melting).
generation.conditions: Nitrogen or He carrier gas, stagnation temperature 350–400 °C, pressure 3–4 MPa, De-Laval nozzle exit velocity 900–1100 m s⁻¹, layer thickness 30 µm, build on room-temperature Cu substrate; manufacture 10 mm × 5 mm × 2 mm dog-bone mini-tensile coupons in air with simple XYZ robot (no pre- or post-heat).
generation.structural_mediator: Severe plastic deformation and adiabatic shear at particle/particle interfaces generate an ultrafine (≤200 nm) dynamically recrystallised microstructure with minimal chemical segregation and no solidification microcracks.
generation.mechanism: Because the powder remains solid, thermal gradients and shrinkage on cooling are suppressed, so macro residual stresses are limited to those from shot-peening-like impact; concurrent high strain-rate deformation work-hardens the HEA and refines grains, increasing strength while preserving ductility; the absence of melt pools removes key sources of processing complexity (laser optics, scan-strategy optimisation, support structures for warpage control).
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to LPBF-built AlCrFeNiSi parts: (a) X-ray diffraction sin²ψ residual-stress values fall from >300 MPa to <50 MPa; (b) 0.2 % proof stress rises from ~0.7 GPa to ≥1.0 GPa, uniform elongation doubles from ~6 % to ≥12 %; (c) post-build distortion decreases from >0.3 mm to <0.05 mm for the stated coupon geometry; surface roughness (Sa) may rise mildly (≈10 µm vs 6 µm).
generation.baseline: Identical coupons fabricated by LPBF at 200 W, 400 mm s⁻¹, 50 µm layers on a 150 °C substrate plate under argon, with no post-build heat treatment.
generation.boundary: Applies to walls or struts ≤3 mm thick; carrier-gas temperature must stay below 0.4·T_m to avoid partial melting; powder must be ductile enough for bonding (oxygen ≤0.15 wt %); effects may diminish for parts >30 mm in height due to cumulative heating.
generation.uncertainty: Densification to >99 % may be challenging for very fine (<15 µm) features; surface finish may require secondary machining; limited published data exist for cold-spray processing of high-entropy alloys, so exact strength gains are estimated.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two groups (n = 6 each) of 10 mm × 5 mm × 2 mm mini-tensile coupons: Group A by LPBF (baseline), Group B by CSAM under the specified parameters. No post-processing except surface cleaning. Compare residual stress, microstructure and mechanical response.
measurements: XRD sin²ψ residual-stress mapping on both faces
Room-temperature uniaxial tensile testing at 10⁻³ s⁻¹
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If Group B shows (i) ≥100 MPa tensile or compressive residual stress OR (ii) <0.9 GPa 0.2 % proof strength OR (iii) <8 % uniform elongation, the hypothesis is falsified.
